question.problem:
Find the truth set of $P(x)⇒Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $R:$ 

- $P(x):$ $3x-1<5$

- $Q(x):$ ${x}^{2}<4$
question.worked_solution:
Since $P(x)⇒Q(x)≡¬P(x)∨Q(x),$ the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇒Q} & ={T}_{¬P∨Q} \\  & ={T}_{¬P}\cup {T}_{Q} \\  & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we note the following:

- To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-1 & <5 \\ 3x & <6 \\ x & <2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is
${T}_{P}=(-\infty ,2).$
As a result, the complement is
${\overset{―}{T}}_{P}=[2,\infty ).$

- To find the the truth set of $Q(x),$ we solve the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & <4 \\ -2 & <x<2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the truth set of $Q(x)$ is 
${T}_{Q}=(-2,2).$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{P⇒Q} & ={\overset{―}{T}}_{P}\cup {T}_{Q} \\  & =[2,\infty )\cup (-2,2) \\  & =(-2,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
